explanation: Processor architectures define the fundamental design and instruction set of a CPU.  RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) and CISC (Complex Instruction Set Computer) represent two distinct approaches. RISC emphasizes a smaller, simpler instruction set with fixed-length instructions, leading to faster execution and simpler hardware. CISC employs a larger, more complex instruction set with variable-length instructions, potentially offering more functionality per instruction but at the cost of slower execution and more complex hardware. The choice between RISC and CISC impacts performance, power consumption, and design complexity.
